atoms.b: By looking at fossils, we can not only learn about ((++extinct external)) organisms of the past, but also about the living things of ((++today yesterday)).

instruction.text: What similarities can you see between the crocodile fossil and the crocodile?

b.sound: Crocodiles have not changed much over time.
Crocodiles have changed a lot over time.

feedback.finish: Fossils have told us that crocodiles haven’t changed much over the 200 million years that they have existed. This is because they have always been well-adapted to their environments.

instruction.text: What similarities can you see between the fish fossil and the shark?

b.sound: Sharks have not changed much over time.
Sharks have changed a lot over time.

feedback.finish: The earliest evidence of sharks comes from a 450-million-year-old fossil. This tells us that sharks are not only older than the dinosaurs, but even older than trees too!

instruction.text: What similarities can you see between the dinosaur fossil and the bird?

feedback.end: There aren’t many similarities, so you might not think these animals are related...

instruction.text: Select the soil to uncover a new fossil.

feedback.end: This is a special type of winged dinosaur called an Archaeopteryx! When this fossil was first discovered, it provided a missing link between dinosaurs and birds, proving that they are related after all.

instruction.text: What similarities can you see between the winged dinosaur fossil and the bird?

b.sound: Modern birds evolved from winged dinosaurs.
They existed at the same time.

text: Over millions of years, a certain subspecies of dinosaur has evolved into the birds of today!
